title: Reticle Inspection - Contamination Detection on 2920 Series
subtitle: Incoming Wafer QC Quality Validation for 3nm Node Manufacturing
author: David Okafor

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the 2920 Series system to detect and classify Contamination defects during incoming wafer qc inspection at the 3nm technology node. The test is conducted at Singapore Fab 7 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 450mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Contamination defects that are critical to yield at the 3nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the 2920 Series platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: 2920 Series
- Inspection Type: Reticle Inspection
- Target Defect: Contamination
- Process Step: Incoming Wafer QC
- Wafer Size: 450mm
- Technology Node: 3nm
- Fab Location: Singapore Fab 7

This test case applies to all 2920 Series systems deployed at Singapore Fab 7 for incoming wafer qc monitoring in the 3nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: 2920 Series
Software Version: v10.0.540
Recipe: RETICLE_INSPECTION_3nm_INCOMING WAFER QC
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Medium (84 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.25μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: 9-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the 2920 Series system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Reticle Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Contamination defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 3nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 49 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 97% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.1% for Reticle Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.97 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-06-25
Wafers Tested: 22
Total Defects Found: 4517
Defect Density: 1437.81 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 3.7%
Capture Rate: 95.2%
Test Duration: 222 minutes
System Uptime: 98.9%

Result Classification: FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The 2920 Series demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Contamination at the 3nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) No significant drift was observed during the test duration.

e) Statistical process control charts showed stable performance over the test period.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Re-tune detection algorithm thresholds for Contamination at 3nm node.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Escalate to R&D for algorithm enhancement if re-tuning does not resolve sensitivity gap.
